blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-migration-1 (`rename_all = "camelCase"` renames every existing order JSON field) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
#[derive(Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct OrderResponse {
    pub order_id: i64,
    pub customer_id: i64,
    pub total_cents: i64,
findings.recommendation: Remove `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` so `GET /orders/{id}` keeps emitting `order_id`, `customer_id` and `total_cents` (the new `currency` field is unaffected either way). Today a partner integration reading `order_id` gets no such field after the deploy and breaks without warning; docs/api.md promises a field is never renamed without two releases of deprecation, and the proposal's release note announces only an addition, with no BREAKING item. If camelCase is really wanted, it needs its own change: emit both names during the deprecation window, mark it BREAKING and announce it.
findings.title: `rename_all = "camelCase"` renames every existing order JSON field

findings.evidence:
/// The currency of orders that do not name one (ISO 4217).
pub default_currency: String,
findings.recommendation: Add `#[serde(default = ...)]` returning "EUR" (the currency the shop sold in before this change) so a deployed `config.toml` holding only `database_url` and `listen` keeps loading; today `load` returns a `missing field default_currency` error and the service fails at start-up after the upgrade. Otherwise document the required new key as a manual upgrade step in the release note. Add a test loading the old two-key config.
findings.title: Existing `config.toml` files without `default_currency` no longer load
